title: A check is one row with one SELECT and its explanation
statement: Each check MUST be one row of the check table, Lathe's in `lathe/data/check.jsonl` and a product's in its own `data/check.jsonl`, with its one-sentence summary, its explanation ending with how to fix what it reports, its severity and the kinds it concerns, and a query that is a single `SELECT` returning `record` and `message`, and `severity` when the check is error_or_warning.

title: Git runs from an argument array
statement: The code MUST run `git` with `spawn` and an array of arguments, with `shell: false`, and MUST NOT build a command string for a shell, so no record ID or path can be read as shell syntax.

title: Built-in modules are imported with the node prefix
statement: The engine, the server, the desktop app and their tests MUST import Node's built-in modules by their `node:` name, such as `node:fs` or `node:child_process`, never by the bare name.

title: Tracked files name no client product, person or machine
statement: A file git tracks in the Lathe repo MUST NOT name a client product Lathe was tried on, a person as a person, or a machine's own paths: no absolute path into a person's home folder or the system's temp folder. A test that needs a home folder MUST use the neutral fake user `/Users/person`; a spec names roles (Owner, Reader, Agent); an example names the idea itself. Only the packages' author and owner fields, the `@jaredrob/lathe` package name and the GitHub owner in the repo's URL name the author. Working notes that name a product, a person or a machine are kept outside the repo.

title: Every check of Lathe's has a test in its domain's folder that breaks it
statement: Each of Lathe's check rows MUST have a test in its domain's test folder (`lathe/test/<domain>/`, such as `lathe/test/checking/` for a check row under LA-CHK) that starts from a product breaking no check and changes one thing to break the check's rule, so a check that stops finding its mistake, or starts finding others, fails a test.

title: A test runs at the lowest level that can observe its result
statement: A test MUST run at the lowest level that can observe its result, cheapest first: unit, integration, service, system, browser. A test SHOULD run a level higher only when the level below cannot observe what it expects, and its notes SHOULD say why. A flow test, a smoke test of its flow's whole path, runs at its interface's level.

title: A Remove takes its record whole and is refused while referenced
statement: Each Remove command MUST take the record it names with everything that sits under it inside its aggregate, their parts and the links they start (for an aggregate's root, the instance whole), and MUST be refused, naming what references them, while anything left still references any of them.

title: Aggregates are small
statement: An aggregate MUST be the smallest cluster of entities that must stay consistent after one command: most hold a root and a few children, and none SHOULD hold more than the product's `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting (7 by default), which `aggregate-too-large` enforces. A rule that spans two aggregates MUST be a specification a command checks, or follow through an event and a policy.

title: A capability is named as a noun phrase for a lasting ability
statement: A capability's title MUST be a noun phrase naming a lasting ability of the business: a subject and an activity noun (Invoice management, Payment processing, Member registration), or a single noun when the area is clear on its own (Catalog, Lending). It MUST say what, not how: it MUST NOT start with an -ing word or with The, and MUST NOT name a screen, a tool or a technology. It SHOULD still be true if the product were rebuilt on other technology, and SHOULD be two to four words. title-breaks-convention warns of the parts a query can read: an -ing word or The first in a title of two or more words, an interface word, and a list.

title: A use case is named for one goal, verb first
statement: A use case's title MUST name one goal of its actor, verb first: an imperative verb and its object, with a qualifier only when needed (Read an invoice, Borrow a tool). It MUST use the domain's own verb (Borrow, Approve, Refund, Model, Declare); Create, Read, Update, Delete, Change or Edit MAY be used only as the domain's own word for its goal, never over a record or data. It MUST name one goal, with no and joining two goals and no list, and MUST NOT name an interface or mechanism (the command line, the desktop app, a page, the command layer): interfaces belong to its flows. It SHOULD be two to six words. title-breaks-convention warns of a title that holds one of its product's interface titles or an interface word, a list, or a CRUD verb over a record or data.

title: Every title is sentence case, unique and without a period
statement: Every record's title MUST be in sentence case, MUST be unique within its kind and product, and MUST NOT end with a period; detail goes in its statement or description. Its length SHOULD fit its family: a name one to four words, a goal two to six, a statement one short sentence of about fifteen words. The store refuses a title another record of its kind and product has, compared trimmed (and in any letter case, except a code-bound kind's identifiers, which compare exactly), with `title-unique`, and one ending with a period with `title-period`.

title: A name is a noun phrase with no article
statement: A product, integration and interface MUST be titled by its proper name (Tool Library, Git, Web app). A domain and capability MUST be a noun for a business area or ability (Lending, Invoice management). An aggregate, entity, value object, term, read model, pattern and standard MUST be a singular noun phrase with no article (Loan, Record ID, Loan history); a domain service a noun phrase for what it works out (Due date, Next ID); a view its subject and form (Loan page, Return dialog); a UI component a noun phrase for what it shows (Record card); a test data set a noun phrase for its contents (Complete example library); and a business outcome the state wanted, as a noun phrase (More tools in use). A name SHOULD be one to four words.

title: A goal starts with its verb
statement: A use case, command and skill MUST be titled by an imperative verb and its object (Borrow a tool). A query MUST start with Get, List or Find and name what it returns (List overdue loans), which `query-title-verb` warns of. A flow MUST be its use case's title, then in or through, then its interface's title (Borrow a tool in the web app, Borrow a tool through the HTTP API), which `flow-title-off-pattern` warns of. A goal SHOULD be two to six words, a flow's the use case's and the interface's together.

title: A happening says what happened or follows
statement: A domain event MUST be a past participle phrase, subject first (Tool borrowed), which `event-tense` warns of. A policy MUST read "When" its event, then its reaction (When a tool is returned damaged, hold it for repair). A flow step MUST name the actor or system and what it does, in the present tense (The member picks a tool).

title: A statement is true when its rule holds
statement: An invariant, constraint, UC, view and API requirement, standard rule and pattern rule MUST be titled by a short sentence that is true when the rule holds (A loan has one borrower). A specification MUST be a yes/no condition with no article (Tool is available), which `specification-title-article` warns of. Every test MUST be titled by the observable result it shows (An overdue loan is refused a renewal), never "Tests that…" or "Should…", which `test-title-not-a-result` warns of.

title: A code-bound title is the identifier in code
statement: A data model, projection, command, query, event and endpoint handler, service, repository, adapter, predicate, value type, table, event type, and a product's code-bound kinds (such as an API client, shared module, entry point, tooling, IPC channel or plugin hook) MUST be titled by the identifier exactly as in code, with no whitespace (`LoanRow`, `buildReference`, `loan`); how it works goes in its description, where its kind has one. An endpoint MUST be its method and route (POST /api/use-case/add-flow-step), a CLI command its invocation (lathe use-case add-flow-step), and a check row the kebab-case name of the mistake (event-tense). The store refuses a title out of its kind's form (meta_kind_title, which a product kind gives as its title_form) with `title-form`, and an endpoint titled other than by its method and route with the endpoint table's CHECK.

title: Every kind's text is required or absent
statement: Every kind MUST have at most one lead text, the column that opens its page: statement for something that must hold, goal for a use case, meaning for a term, field or setting, description for a thing that is. A lead MUST be required (NOT NULL and never blank), and MUST say what the title, the parent, the links and the facts cannot, never restating another record. A kind whose record only implements another in the domain layer (data model, value type, predicate, event type, service) and a flow, flow step or table have none. A test's scenario MUST give When and Then, with any setup opening its When; its shared starting state is the test data set it starts from. A product kind's lead is a field named statement, goal, meaning or description: at most one, and required, or the store refuses the declaration (`product-kind`).

title: Mistakes are refused, not found
statement: Lathe MUST refuse data and changes that break its model when they are made, not report them afterwards; a rule that can be enforced when something is written MUST be enforced then (poka-yoke: make illegal states unrepresentable).

title: One way to do each thing
statement: Lathe MUST offer one way to do each thing (standard work: one obvious way): one command for each intent on an aggregate, each rule written once, in the code of what it governs, and each interface naming the one command it runs.

title: No exceptions
statement: Every rule MUST hold everywhere it applies, with no exception, waiver, exemption or recorded deviation. Where a rule does not fit a case, the model or the code MUST change until the case meets it, or the rule MUST change everywhere at once (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES-R04).

title: Change the standard, not the instance
statement: When the standard way proves wrong, it MUST be changed everywhere at once (a hard cutover, with no aliases or old forms kept), not worked around in one place; what no longer serves a purpose MUST be removed.

title: Main is wholly traced and clean
statement: On every merge into main, `lathe check` on Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library MUST count 100% of their obligations designed, built and proved, summed over every domain, and MUST print 0 errors and 0 warnings; a merge that misses either MUST NOT land.
